title: A check that sees several jobs at once

blocks.text: A water utility's pipe program passes every single-job check: no required job, alone, costs more than the money it could use. Yet the model has no plan. The program's budget rolls over: money not spent in a year is added to the next year's. Each job is paid in full in the year it is done, and a required job must be done by the end of its `deadline` year.

So, by the end of any year $`y`$, the program must have paid for every required job whose deadline is $`y`$ or earlier, and it cannot have paid more than all the budgets up to $`y`$. A year where the first sum is larger than the second proves there is no plan, whatever else the model says. That is a check on several jobs at once, which the single-job checks cannot see.

Write `cumulative_check(items, budget)`. `items` maps a job name to `{"cost", "deadline", "required"}`, and `budget` maps each plan year to its budget ($k). Return a list of `(year, due, available)` triples, in year order, one for every year where the required work due by the end of that year costs more than the money available by then. Return `[]` when no year falls short. About ten lines.

cases.says: a year in which the required work due so far costs more than all the money so far is reported, with both sums
a shortfall can last more than one year, and each year is reported
unspent money rolls into the next year, so the money available grows year by year
only required work is ever due

origin.section: Passing Every Check Does Not Mean a Plan Exists

concepts: a sound check over several jobs at once, with money that rolls over
